generation_metadata.agent_last_message:
The implementation is complete and thoroughly verified. Here's a summary of what was built:

## Summary

A complete RS274/NGC G-code simulator in C++20 at `output/` (24 source files, builds cleanly with `cmake -B build && cmake --build build`, zero warnings with `-Wall -Wextra`).

**Coverage:** full expression evaluator (parameters, binary/unary ops, precedence), all G-codes (motion, arcs in both radius/center format, canned cycles G81–G89, cutter radius compensation with tangent-circle entry construction, tool length offsets, coordinate systems, G92 family, G28/G30, G38.2 probing), all M-codes, the complete Table 8 order-of-execution, tool-table and parameter-file I/O, and the full trace-file engine (time/distance/tolerance-adaptive stepping, sub-motion decomposition, delta encoding, the nuanced label-attachment and conflict-resolution rules).

**Validation approach:** I verified against every worked example embedded in the spec itself (the three trace examples, the G81 sticky-parameter examples, the Table 12 cutter-comp program, the full Appendix C sample programs) as ground truth, plus ~65 hand-written test cases covering error conditions, edge cases, and unit/plane/distance-mode interactions. I also commissioned two independent adversarial code reviews (one on core interpreter semantics, one on trace/CRC/output generation), which caught and led to fixes for two real bugs (G4 miscategorized into the wrong modal group, causing crashes; incremental-mode canned-cycle depth computed relative to the wrong reference point) — both confirmed against the spec's own worked examples before and after the fix.

**Documented judgment calls:** a few spec ambiguities required interpretation (default path-control/canned-return modal state, P/Q stickiness for canned cycles, and several genuinely hard corners of cutter radius compensation under the tool-tip-relative semantics from Clarifications.md). These are recorded in code comments and in a project memory file, in case future t

comparison.note: Same node IDs can have corrected fixtures/assertions; transitions describe these rubric revisions, not repeated trials of an unchanged test suite.

provenance.availability: Portable score summary, not a complete regrade bundle. Raw regrade JSON, source/test snapshots and pytest reports were produced in a scratch working directory on the auditing workstation and are not committed.
